data.narrative:
MightyFly, founded by Manal Habib, is a Series A–stage drone and autonomous systems company that has raised $10M to date. The Drones & Autonomous sector comprises eight private peers including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air, with no public comparables available for direct benchmarking.

Given the early-stage nature and limited peer visibility at identical stage and valuation tier, only one valuation method proved applicable. Stage-Progression analysis uses the $10M total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A advancement to subsequent rounds, yielding a $20M implied valuation. Peer-Median comparison was not feasible due to insufficient narrow-set peers meeting simultaneous filters for stage, tier, and sector alignment—though five same-sector companies exist, none formed a cohort of three or more at comparable stage and scale.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $17M (low) to $23M (high), with a median point of $20M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodological pillar; the primary uncertainty stems from the sparse comparable universe in early-stage autonomous systems, which limits external validation of the stage-progression assumption. Investor conviction in this valuation should be weighted toward company-specific fundamentals—technology differentiation, market timing, and founding team track record—rather than sector multiples.
